# Save fixtures

One frozen save per schema version. `save-v<n>.json` is what `toSave` wrote at version `n`.

- `save-v0.json`: the bare state from the clock ticket (#4), `version: 0`, no envelope. Derived from `save-v1.json` by hand: the same world, unwrapped.
- `save-v1.json`: `{ format, version: 1, world }` (#8). Seed 8, 1,200 ticks, plus hand-filled lambs, a shear timer, a farmer with a plan, small life, and a queued intent.
- `save-v2.json`: same envelope, `version: 2` (#5 part a). Same seed and build recipe as v1, so the world also has DL's five behaviour-chain fields (`stick`, `circleUntilMs`, `dirAtMs`, `tagUntilMs`, `forceBoundUntilMs`); v1 saves get them filled with fresh-state defaults by the v2 migration.
- `save-v3.json`: same envelope, `version: 3` (#5 part b). Same seed and build recipe again; the world has `nameIdx` and the farmer has the eight NPC job-plan fields (`wp`, `outside`, `entering`, `job`, `shearing`, `cart`, `icon`, `iconUntilMs`). The sheep, DL, and the NPCs now move during the 1,200 ticks, so the world is not v2 plus those fields. v1 and v2 saves get `nameIdx` (the flock size) and the NPC fields (`makeNpc`'s spawn values) filled by the v3 migration.
- `save-v4.json`: same envelope, `version: 4` (#33). Same seed and build recipe, plus two hand-placed snow prints; the world has `ground` (`prints`, `mud`, `wasSnowy`), and each sheep and DL have `lastStamp` and `stampSide`. The mud is real: the shower's walk to the barn stamped it. The bird now rolls every tick and the butterflies drift, so the 1,200 ticks are a different 1,200 ticks than v3's. Older saves get an empty ground and unstamped walkers filled by the v4 migration.
- `save-v5.json`: same envelope, `version: 5` (#39). Same seed and build recipe; the world has `ledger` (the district's numbers as the Ledger path last wrote them: here the snapshot `createInitialState` took, older than the world around it) and `lastLedgerAt` (0, its clock then). The 1,200 ticks are the same 1,200 ticks as v4's: the Ledger is a new path, not a change to the tick. A v4 save gets its snapshot read off its own world by the v5 migration, stamped with the world's clock.
- `save-v6.json`: same envelope, `version: 6` (#60). Same seed and build recipe, plus two hand-placed chronicle entries (a 'ledger' line with only a numeric fact and no actors, an 'authored' line with a hint, an actor, and a string fact) so the fixture covers every type on `ChronicleEntry`. The 1,200 ticks are the same 1,200 ticks as v5's: the chronicle is a new path, not a change to the tick. A v5 save gets a fresh, empty chronicle filled in by the v6 migration: it never kept one, so there is no history to recover.
- `save-v7.json`: same envelope, `version: 7` (#40). Same seed and build recipe, and the 1,200 ticks now run with the event engine directing, so the world is not v6 plus a field: the merchant's visit is a card draw rather than his fixed timer, and the two chronicle entries the recipe places by hand sit after the ones the engine told. On top of that, the engine's corners are filled by hand — one card running, another id on cooldown with its start behind it, a flag, a mood offset, a remembered shower, and the lamb that card walked off its mother's trail (`lost: true` plus the `lostLamb` marker pointing at it) — so the fixture covers every type on `EventsState`. A v6 save gets a fresh engine, seeded from its own `seed` and stamped with its own clock, filled in by the v7 migration: it never had one, and nothing in a v6 world says what would have been running.

- `save-v8.json`: same envelope, `version: 8` (#84). Same seed and build recipe, and the 1,200 ticks are the same 1,200 ticks as v7's: the real-year calendar is two more numbers on `season`, not a change to the tick. `world.season` and the Ledger snapshot's own `ledger.season` each carry `realEpochMs` (1775001600000, i.e. 2026-04-01T00:00:00Z — `DEFAULT_REAL_EPOCH_MS`, what a world created without a real time from the host gets) and `seed` (8, the world's own). A v7 save has neither and no record of what they would have been, so the v8 migration anchors it to **the real present at its first load**: `fromSave(doc, { realNowMs })`, epoch `realNowMs - season.elapsedMs`, so the world's real date comes out as exactly `realNowMs` that once and is a deterministic function of the stored number from then on. A caller that passes no real time (every test here) gets `DEFAULT_REAL_EPOCH_MS`, which is why this fixture is byte-stable. The snapshot gets the *same* epoch as the world, not one of its own: it is the same world at an earlier moment and its own `elapsedMs` already carries the difference.

Rules:

- Never edit or regenerate an existing fixture. It is the frozen input the migration chain must keep loading.
- When `SAVE_VERSION` bumps: add the migration under `src/save/migrations`, list it in `MIGRATIONS`, run `npm run test -w packages/sim`. `test/save-fixture.test.ts` writes the missing `save-v<new>.json` from `buildFixtureState()`; commit it.
- Every fixture in this folder is loaded and stepped 100 ticks on every test run.
